# 1.5 Association: learning what is bad {#sec-association}

<div data-life="status" data-stage="1.5"></div>

::: {.callout-warning title="On hold: the learning rule is being redesigned"}
The figures below come from runs of an older design, made under different settings, and the seeds are not
comparable with each other: they were scored with different measures of fitness. Do not read results from them.

The rule in those runs only ever raised the weights onto the aversive cells: pain taught "what I just bit is
bad", and nothing taught "that was fine after all". All berries share part of their look, so suspicion of a
poison berry spread to the good ones and was never taken back, and the animals ended up eating less of
everything. The next design adds a cell that fires when the animal expected something bad and the bite turned out
fine, and lowers the weights again.

The text of this page will be written when the stage is frozen.
:::

Some kinds of berry now look different in every life, so no inherited synapse can know them. Pain teaches the
synapses from what was just bitten to the aversive cells.
